project.name: Fleet Planner
project.purpose: Daily tool that fills in Driver and Vehicle columns of an uploaded Excel transport-request file, using a deterministic rules engine plus an optional AI review layer, then exports the same file with only those two columns changed.
project.status: actively developed, core pipeline working and validated against real user data

folder_structure.fleetplanner.db: SQLite database, created at runtime; a real snapshot has also been committed to the linked repo for AI testing purposes
folder_structure.app/db.py: all SQLite schema, migrations, and CRUD
folder_structure.app/rules_parser.py: free-text rule-line recognizer, used ONLY for AI-context notes, not hard rules
folder_structure.app/excel_import.py: daily request-file reader, produces Job objects
folder_structure.app/export.py: writes results into a copy of the original uploaded workbook
folder_structure.app/ui/main_window.py: QMainWindow, tab container, Settings PIN gating
folder_structure.app/ui/plan_day_tab.py: daily workflow screen, largest UI file
folder_structure.app/ui/drivers_tab.py: structured driver hard rules + AI notes
folder_structure.app/ui/vehicles_tab.py: vehicle roster, workshop/exclusion toggle, edit dialog
folder_structure.app/ui/settings_tab.py: API keys, PIN, digest refresh control

modules.responsibility: The deterministic core. No AI, no network calls, fully repeatable. Takes in-memory profiles + jobs, mutates jobs in place.
modules.does_not_import: app.db at module level -- db is passed as an explicit parameter to build_*_profiles functions, keeping this module testable standalone

dataclasses.name: DriverProfile
dataclasses.critical_history_note: shift_start field was OMITTED from this dataclass during an earlier rewrite -- a real bug, fixed. Any future field additions to drivers must be added here too, not just in the database.

dataclasses.name: VehicleProfile
fields: in_workshop (bool, merged from db.in_workshop OR db.excluded_from_planning)

dataclasses.name: SupplierHire
dataclasses.computed_property: label -- supplier_name if instance_number==1 else f'{supplier_name} {instance_number-1}'
dataclasses.note: RUNTIME ONLY, created dynamically during allocate(), never stored directly in the database -- only the resulting label text and supplier_id get persisted via finalized_jobs on Finalize

key_functions.name: build_driver_profiles
key_functions.purpose: reads drivers table, skips excluded_from_planning, computes month_overtime_so_far via db.get_driver_month_overtime_hours

key_functions.name: build_supplier_offerings
key_functions.purpose: reads supplier_offerings joined with suppliers, computes cumulative_hours_history via db.get_supplier_cumulative_hours

key_functions.name: _driver_qualifies_for_type
key_functions.purpose: exact-match check against license_types list; returns False entirely if license_types is empty (forces explicit configuration)

key_functions.name: _driver_is_off
key_functions.purpose: weekday check against off_days, with allow_override_days escape hatch

key_functions.name: _parse_shift_start_time
key_functions.purpose: parses '07:00 AM' or '18:00' style text into datetime.time

key_functions.name: _job_is_before_shift_start
key_functions.purpose: hard rule: job.start_dt.time() must not be earlier than driver's parsed shift_start

key_functions.name: _overlaps_with_buffer
key_functions.purpose: checks time-interval overlap with a configurable minute buffer (default 30) for travel time between jobs

key_functions.name: _type_matches
key_functions.purpose: case-insensitive, whitespace-normalized EXACT string comparison -- no fuzzy matching, deliberate design choice

key_functions.name: allocate
key_functions.signature: allocate(jobs, drivers, vehicles, supplier_offerings, allowed_driver_ids=None, allowed_supplier_ids=None, allow_override_days=None, travel_buffer_minutes=30)
key_functions.algorithm_summary: For each job in time order: try in-house (qualifying + not off + shift started + no overlap + no overtime violation, pick least-occupied-hours candidate, then find any free matching vehicle). If no in-house driver+vehicle combo found, try supplier: prefer reusing an already-hired unit from today (any matching offering) that's free; if none, hire a new unit from the offering with lowest cumulative_hours_history among those with remaining daily capacity, naming it via SupplierHire.label convention.
key_functions.note_on_unused_params: allowed_driver_ids and allowed_supplier_ids support a 'restrict to shortlist' feature that has NO UI control yet -- backend-ready, frontend not built

modules.fairness_model: hours-occupied, not job-count. min(candidates, key=lambda d: d.occupied_seconds)

supplier_naming_convention.priority: always try to reuse an already-hired unit before hiring a new one, to minimize headcount for the day
supplier_naming_convention.note: user's own historical manually-planned reference files are inconsistent about this numbering (some suppliers numbered, some not) -- confirmed by user this is a manual-entry artifact, NOT the desired behavior; the engine's consistent numbering is correct and should not be changed to match old files

overtime_model.max_overtime_hours_per_month_zero: no overtime allowed at all -- working_hours_per_day becomes a strict daily ceiling
overtime_model.max_overtime_hours_per_month_positive: monthly overtime budget, checked against finalized_jobs history

modules.responsibility: One job: HTTP call to Google Routes API, parse response, raise MapsClientError on failure. Knows nothing about jobs/drivers/allocation.

key_functions.name: get_travel_time
key_functions.raises: MapsClientError on any failure (missing key, bad response, no route found)
key_functions.important_detail: uses routingPreference=TRAFFIC_AWARE and passes the job's ACTUAL departure time (converted to RFC3339 UTC via _to_rfc3339) -- this is why the same route can return different estimates depending on time of day, which was an explicit requirement

modules.responsibility: Builds AI context payload, calls Claude, parses JSON response into suggestions. Never mutates a Job directly -- only returns suggestion dicts.

key_functions.name: build_review_context
key_functions.signature: build_review_context(jobs, event_groups, driver_hours_summary, travel_time_lookups, day_notes, preferences_digest='')
key_functions.returns: dict with keys: events_with_multiple_stages, driver_occupied_hours_today, travel_time_lookups_minutes, planner_day_notes, planner_preferences_digest
key_functions.note: filters event_groups to only events with >=2 stages -- single-stage events have nothing to reason about

key_functions.name: review_plan
key_functions.returns: list[suggestion dict] with keys: type, affected_jobs, reasoning
key_functions.note: defensively strips markdown code fences from the response before JSON parsing, since the model sometimes wraps output despite instructions not to

system_prompt_responsibilities: reason about event-chain stay-on-site vs cycle-back decisions using travel time + gap + driver remaining hours
weigh travel-time confidence (exact vs approximate, from Locations tab resolution) -- more conservative suggestions on approximate data
read planner day-notes and propose specific overrides only when clearly supported
flag conflicts revealed by real travel times
use planner_preferences_digest as guidance, not a hard rule
NEVER change the plan itself -- suggestions only
respond ONLY with valid JSON matching the fixed suggestion schema

modules.responsibility: Compresses decision_log into the small preference_digest. Planner-triggered only (Settings tab button), never automatic -- deliberate cost control.

key_functions.name: refresh_digest
key_functions.behavior: reads db.get_decisions_since(conn, existing_digest.covered_through_date); if empty, returns existing digest UNCHANGED and makes ZERO API calls (verified by test, not just intent); otherwise sends existing digest + only the new decisions to Claude, saves the merged result with an updated covered_through_date watermark
key_functions.cost_guarantee: old decisions are never resent on subsequent refreshes -- confirmed via test with decisions across multiple dates and two refresh calls

modules.responsibility: Loads the ORIGINAL uploaded workbook, writes only Vehicle/Driver columns for matched rows, saves as a new file. Regenerates nothing.

key_functions.behavior: openpyxl.load_workbook(original_path) preserves all styles/formatting; finds Vehicle/Driver column indices by header text; for each job matched by row_number, writes driver_text (driver name, or supplier label if supplier-assigned) and vehicle_text (plate, or blank for supplier jobs) into ONLY those two cells; unresolved jobs get both left blank
key_functions.verified: tested against a real file -- confirmed row/column counts unchanged, header font/formatting unchanged, an untouched column (Event) byte-identical before/after

business_rules: In-house drivers/vehicles are always attempted before any supplier for every job, independently, in time order -- no pre-reservation of jobs for suppliers.
Fairness among in-house drivers is measured by cumulative occupied HOURS, not job count.
A driver's license_types must contain an EXACT (case/whitespace-normalized) match for a job's vehicle_type_required, or the driver is not considered at all for that job.
A job starting before a driver's configured shift_start can never be assigned to that driver.
Off days are a hard skip unless explicitly overridden for a specific date (allow_override_days parameter, no UI yet).
max_overtime_hours_per_month: NULL/blank = unlimited overtime; 0 = no overtime allowed at all; positive number = monthly budget checked against finalized_jobs history.
Supplier hiring always tries to REUSE an already-hired unit before hiring a new one, to minimize the day's headcount, even if it means one supplier driver works more hours.
New supplier hires are chosen from the offering with the LOWEST cumulative historical hours among suppliers with remaining daily capacity, for cross-day fairness.

Supplier unit naming: 1st hire = bare supplier name, 2nd hire = 'NAME 1', Nth = 'NAME {N-1}', reuse = 'SAME <label>'. This is user-confirmed and should not be changed based on old inconsistent manual reference files.
A vehicle is unavailable if EITHER in_workshop OR excluded_from_planning is set -- they are treated as equivalent for allocation purposes.
AI suggestions never change the plan automatically -- every suggestion requires an explicit planner Accept/Reject click.

The raw decision_log is never sent to Claude -- only the small, periodically-refreshed preference_digest is included in daily AI Review calls, to keep cost/latency flat over time regardless of history length.
Export must preserve the original uploaded file exactly, changing only the Vehicle and Driver cell values for matched rows -- no reformatting, no regeneration from a template.
Unresolved jobs (no valid assignment found) are never written to finalized_jobs.
Events (grouped by event_id) with 2+ stages are the unit of reasoning for the AI's stay-on-site-vs-cycle-back judgment; single-stage events are excluded from that reasoning entirely.

workflows.name: daily_planning_workflow
steps: 1. Upload Excel file -> excel_import.load_jobs_from_excel -> list[Job] in memory
3. Run Planning -> allocation_engine.allocate() mutates jobs -> results table rendered, filter dropdown populated
4. (optional) AI Review -> travel-time lookups via maps_client + db.resolve_location -> ai_review.review_plan() -> suggestion cards with Accept/Reject
5. (per suggestion) Accept/Reject -> db.log_decision (does NOT auto-update the table -- known gap)
6. Finalize Day -> db.save_finalized_jobs (skips unresolved jobs, overwrites existing rows for that date)
7. Export Filled Excel -> export.export_filled_excel writes into a COPY of the original file, saved wherever the planner chooses

workflows.name: digest_refresh_workflow
workflows.trigger: manual, planner clicks 'Refresh Preferences Digest Now' in Settings tab
steps: 1. db.get_digest -> existing digest text + covered_through_date watermark
3. If none new: return existing digest unchanged, ZERO API calls made
4. If new decisions exist: send existing digest + new decisions to Claude, get merged/updated digest text (capped ~400 words)
5. db.save_digest with new watermark = latest decision's plan_date

workflows.name: master_data_setup_workflow
workflows.description: one-time-ish setup, edited only when something changes (new driver, rate change, vehicle to workshop)

architectural_decisions.decision: Standalone single-user desktop app, not multi-user web app
architectural_decisions.reasoning: Only one planner uses the actual software; supervisor/drivers only ever see the exported file distributed externally. Eliminated need for hosting/accounts/real-time sync entirely.

architectural_decisions.decision: Deterministic engine and AI review are two separate, manually-triggered steps, not automatically combined
architectural_decisions.reasoning: While the deterministic engine was (and still is, to some degree) being actively debugged, keeping AI out of the automatic loop made every discovered issue traceable to one layer or the other. A combined one-click shortcut is a deliberately deferred future addition.

architectural_decisions.decision: AI never finalizes anything automatically -- suggestions require explicit Accept/Reject
architectural_decisions.reasoning: Non-negotiable requirement from the first design discussion; human stays in control of every change.

architectural_decisions.decision: Two-tier decision history: full local log (never sent) + small periodically-refreshed digest (only thing sent)
architectural_decisions.reasoning: Answers 'does the AI learn over time' honestly (the model is stateless per call) while letting the SYSTEM reflect accumulated real decisions without unbounded cost/latency growth.

architectural_decisions.decision: Hard rules moved from free-text rule-line parsing to structured database columns
architectural_decisions.reasoning: Directly caused by two real bugs (a driver's hour cap silently unenforced due to un-matched phrasing; later, shift_start type of issue) where free-text matching failed silently. Structured fields with explicit format-hint UI eliminate the ambiguity.

architectural_decisions.decision: Supplier units are generated dynamically at planning time, never pre-named by the planner
architectural_decisions.reasoning: The original 'pre-name your trucks' model was identified as backwards -- the app should decide unit numbering based on actual daily demand, not have the planner guess in advance.

architectural_decisions.decision: Export loads and modifies the ORIGINAL workbook rather than regenerating from a template
architectural_decisions.reasoning: Explicit requirement: output must be byte-identical to the input except for the Vehicle/Driver cells -- no reformatting risk.

architectural_decisions.decision: Settings PIN disables the tab entirely rather than switch-then-revert
architectural_decisions.reasoning: The switch-then-revert approach could flash tab contents before the check completed -- a real, observed issue, fixed by disabling the tab outright while locked.

architectural_decisions.decision: Additive-only schema migrations (ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN)
architectural_decisions.reasoning: After multiple rounds of asking the user to delete their local database for schema changes, this was added so small future field additions don't cause data loss. Structural changes (rename/retype/remove) still require a fresh database.

architectural_decisions.decision: Vehicle-type matching is exact string comparison, never fuzzy
architectural_decisions.reasoning: Deliberately rejected fuzzy matching as riskier than the problem it solves (risk of silently conflating genuinely different vehicle configurations). Real-world text mismatches are treated as a data-entry/process problem to fix at the source, not a matching-algorithm problem to work around.

real_world_validation_performed.method: user pushed a real fleetplanner.db snapshot plus a real day's UNPLANNED.xlsx/PLANNED.xlsx pair to a public GitHub repo specifically for AI testing
findings_were_mostly_data_issues_not_cod: All 11 drivers in the snapshot had identical license_types ('5 Ton Chiller Truck (with lift)'), blocking 95 of 125 real jobs from ever going in-house
Only 4 in-house chiller trucks existed in the snapshot, 2 legitimately locked for a full 12-hour event
A driver (VENUGOPAL) present in the planned reference was missing from the database entirely
A vehicle-type text mismatch ('23 Seater Bus' entered vs '23 Seated Bus' required) caused a silent zero-match
real_world_validation_performed.code_bug_found_via_this_process: shift_start field missing from DriverProfile dataclass -- see allocation_engine module entry above
real_world_validation_performed.tooling_built_during_validation: a one-off script extracting suggested license_types per driver directly from PLANNED.xlsx by grouping historical Driver->VehicleType pairs; applied to a test database copy, improved match rate from 4% to 7% (confirming license types were a real factor but not the sole explanation)
